articles.headline: Cucurella: Too soon to judge Mourinho's Madrid amid poor start
articles.description: Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.
articles.body:
Marc Cucurella has acknowledged Real Madrid have not started the season as they would have liked under new coach José Mourinho, but he says the team must be judged at the end of the campaign, not now.

Madrid have suffered two defeats in their opening seven LaLiga games, against Real Betis and Atlético Madrid, leaving them six points behind early leaders Barcelona.

- Torres forced out of Spain squad; Madrid's Espí gets 1st call-up

- De la Fuente says beloved Yamal puts 'magic' at service of Spain

- UEFA receives Madrid dossier on Barça-Negreira case

Cucurella, speaking in a news conference on Friday while on international duty with world champions Spain, said Madrid's new project needs time to take shape.

"It's all a process," Cucurella said. "With the national team, the foundations have been laid over many years -- with the [same] coach, too.

"At Madrid, we have just started with a new manager and it's too soon to speak. Some players only had a week-long preseason before starting.

"The beginning of the season hasn't been what we all hoped for, but it's a process and we will see where we are at the end of the campaign."

Cucurella has picked up where he left off for Spain at the World Cup in the summer, impressing in UEFA Nations League victories over England and Croatia during the last week.

It has led to suggestions the left back -- a €55 million ($62m) summer signing for Madrid from Chelsea -- is better suited to playing for his country than his club.

"It's not even been 10 games yet," Cucurella responded. "There are things to improve [with Madrid], of course. We basically had no preseason, while it's a new club for me.

"I have to adapt to my new teammates and give my best so that the player you see with the national team is the same player with Real Madrid."

Cucurella's form for Chelsea and Spain not only prompted Madrid to sign him in the summer, but also led to him being named among the 30 nominees to win this year's Ballon d'Or.

He is also in the rare position of playing alongside two of the favourites -- Kylian Mbappé with Madrid and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal with Spain -- but would not pick between the two.

"If it was up to me to vote, I would vote for myself," he joked when asked to name his winner.

"But no, two of the candidates to win it are teammates, so who whoever wins it, I will be happy."

Cucurella and Spain are back in action on Saturday when they host Czechia in Oviedo looking to make it three wins from three in the Nations League.

They then close the extended international break with a trip to Croatia on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Vikings' Justin Jefferson out vs. Dolphins with ankle injury
articles.description: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson won't play against the Dolphins because of a sprained left ankle, but coach Kevin O'Connell is hopeful he can return in Week 5 vs. the Saints.
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson won't play Sunday against the Miami Dolphins because of a sprained left ankle, coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday.

Jefferson did not practice this week after suffering what O'Connell has called a relatively mild injury in the first quarter of the Vikings' victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3.

O'Connell said Jefferson is "definitely feeling better" and did not rule out a return for next week's game at the New Orleans Saints. He has 13 catches for 179 yards and two touchdowns in three games this season.

"We'll see how he comes in," O'Connell said after Friday's practice. "He's going to get treatment throughout the next couple days and the goal is try to get him back out there practicing next week. I know it's a big one for him next week going to Louisiana."

Jefferson was born in St. Rose, Louisiana, and he played collegiately at LSU.

He had played in 39 consecutive games since a torn right hamstring had sidelined him for seven games in 2023. Prior to that, he had played in 55 consecutive games.

With Jefferson sidelined, Jordan Addison is likely to be the Vikings' top target against the Dolphins. He caught five passes for 90 yards and a touchdown after Jefferson's injury. The Vikings' three receiver sets will include Addison, Jauan Jennings and either Myles Price or Tai Felton.

The 2020 first-round pick led the NFL in receiving yards per game (96.5) from 2020-24, but his production dipped dramatically in 2025 as the Vikings tried to develop quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Playing with McCarthy for 10 games and rookie Max Brosmer for two, Jefferson finished the season with a career-low average of 61.6 yards per game.

The Vikings had high hopes of a resurgence in 2026 after signing new starting quarterback Kyler Murray, but they have played only 18 snaps together this season due to Jefferson's ankle injury and a concussion that Murray suffered in Week 1.

articles.headline: Aaron Donald out, Puka Nacua to play in Rams' game vs. Eagles
articles.description: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald will not play against the Eagles as he deals with back soreness, while wide receiver Puka Nacua will return from a hip injury after missing the past two games.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald will not play Sunday against the Eagles as he deals with back soreness, coach Sean McVay said Friday.

The Rams will get wide receiver Puka Nacua back from a hip injury after he missed the past two games.

Donald, who came out of retirement in late August, has played 56% of the defensive snaps in the two games he has played this season. Donald "felt some soreness" in his back after the Rams' Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos, McVay said.

"I think our job as coaches is [to] put our players in positions to have successful outcomes," McVay said. "He's as tough as it gets, just not feeling good enough. And I think it would be irresponsible on my part -- and obviously talking with [team doctor] Reggie [Scott] -- to ask him. He would do it and he could probably go be productive, but part of our job is to protect these tough dudes like him from themselves.

"... He's working as hard as he can to get himself feeling as good as possible. And we're hopeful and optimistic that good days are ahead."

McVay said Nacua will not have an injury designation but the team is still working through how much the wide receiver will play. Nacua has been dealing with the injury since Sept. 17 when he noticed during practice that he felt some pain when trying to change direction on the field.

"Physically he's getting in and out of his breaks, looks strong, looks sturdy, looks explosive," McVay said. "I think it'll really just be a feel for the overall conditioning. Hoping the magic of the jersey on Sundays, he's feeling real good there."

McVay said Nacua "looked sharp" during practice Thursday, when the Rams have their heaviest workload.

"I thought he handled it well," McVay said. "In terms of the snap count, that's the thing that we have to be willing to navigate. But we've got confidence in some other guys that have played meaningful snaps in his absence. But he does look good. He looks strong, and he looks ready to go."

In the season opener, Nacua had five catches for 74 yards.

The Rams also ruled out tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), while tight end Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) is questionable.

articles.headline: Fantasy football rankings for Week 4: IDP
articles.description: Weekly fantasy football draft rankings for IDP leagues from Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.
articles.body:
Each week during the 2026 NFL season, these fantasy football IDP rankings will be updated by fantasy analysts Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.

We've split up our fantasy football rankings by traditional IDP (individual defensive players) positions: defensive line, linebacker and defensive back. Scoring systems can vary greatly in IDP formats, so these rankings are based on the following scoring criteria:

Solo tackle: 1.5 points

Assisted tackle: 0.75 points

Tackle for loss: 2 points

Sack: 4 points

Interception: 5 points

Forced fumble: 4 points

Fumble recovery: 4 points

Defensive TD: 6 points

Safety: 2 points

Pass defensed: 1.5 points

articles.headline: Miami Heat announce 'A Night in Vice City' theme ahead of GTA VI release
articles.description: With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat have been carefully leaning into "Vice City" branding for years now, but 2026 will bring the team's most ambitious effort yet: Nov. 18 will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center.

With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.

Miami is rolling out plenty of offerings for the night. The night will feature a special Vice-themed court and a reimagined edition of the team's popular alternate uniforms, as well as "special game night activities" and "unique game night activations."

According to a news release, the special occasion will "transform the Kaseya Center into Vice City -- showcasing the Miami-inspired setting of Grand Theft Auto VI -- for a first-of-its-kind sports crossover experience."

The Heat kicked off the promotion for the special event Thursday, lighting up "Welcome to Vice City" signage on the roof of the Kaseya Center. The team says it will share more information about "A Night in Vice City" in the coming weeks in coordination with Rockstar Games.

The Heat's game that night against the Milwaukee Bucks will be broadcast on ESPN.

articles.headline: New signing Carlos Baleba gets 1st Man United outing in friendly
articles.description: Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.
articles.body:
Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.

The 22-year-old signed from Brighton in a £70 million ($93m) deal in August but has not featured in a competitive game due to an ankle injury sustained in preseason with the Seagulls.

He did make the bench for the 1-1 draw at Fulham immediately prior to the international break and has continued working towards full fitness at the club's Carrington training complex.

Baleba took part in a training game against Swiss side Lausanne-Sport alongside fellow first-teamers including Harry Maguire and Matheus Cunha.

Head coach Michael Carrick told club media recently that Baleba was "pushing to get back as quickly as possible" from injury.

articles.headline: Erik ten Hag 'was a piece of crap' with Man United squad - Fred
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a 'piece of crap' when it came to squad management.
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a "piece of crap" when it came to squad management.

The Brazilian spent five years at United, winning the League Cup and reaching the FA Cup final in the 2022-23 season.

Ten Hag came to United with a big reputation, having managed Ajax for four seasons and taking them to the Champions League semifinals but, while he did win the FA Cup and League Cup in his two-and-a-half years in Manchester, things did not quite go as planned with regards to success in the Premier League.

And Fred, who left the club to join Turkish side Fenerbahce during Ten Hag's tenure ahead of the 2023-24 season, gave a damning review of his time under the Dutchman.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," he said on the "Charla Podcast."

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

- Sir Alex Ferguson on David Beckham's Preston loan: 'He thought I wanted him gone but that's not true'

- Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery

- Rasmus Højlund hits 'Siuuu' against Portugal: 'Cristiano Ronaldo will never be forgotten'

"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."

Ronaldo left the club at the end of the 2022 season after he found himself no longer in the starting lineup.

Ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, with United 14th after seven matches -- their worst start since the 1989-90 season.

Fred also lifted the lid on other United managers he experienced, including Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the 1999 treble winner who took the helm at the club in December 2018 after Jose Mourinho was sacked.

The 33-year-old, who has 32 Brazil caps, gave his assessment of both of those managers, who he had much more positive things to say about.

"Solskjaer was good with the group, but he was helped [in training] by the assistants. He united the group," Fred added.

"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahçe; he brought me to United.

"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].

"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."
